selection_reason: user-controlled commit messages and file names -> modified escaping function -> constructs quoted and escaped strings for command execution
source_summary: message and files parameters passed to git.commit, originating from CLI arguments (commitMessage via -m flag) and file list from package.json files.
sink_summary: Escaped strings are concatenated into shell commands passed to child_process.exec for git add, git commit -m, git tag -a -m.
guard_summary: escapeQuotes attempts to escape characters ["'$`\] by prefixing with backslash, then wraps the whole string in double quotes. No other validation or sanitization observed on the path from CLI arguments to exec.
risk_pattern: User-controlled commit message and file names are escaped and quoted, then embedded directly into shell command strings executed via child_process.exec, creating a command injection risk if escaping is insufficient for the shell context.
context_summary: escapeQuotes is used in git.commit to escape the commit message and file names before constructing git shell commands. The escaping pattern targets characters that are special in shell double-quoted strings, but the safety depends on the shell's parsing rules and whether the escaping is complete for the intended context.
unresolved_facts: Exact shell environment where git commands run (sh, bash, etc.)
Whether the escaping is sufficient to prevent injection in all targeted shells
Whether there are any other callers of escapeQuotes besides git.commit
